author: Edward Easton
title: 'I was manipulated into blinding myself by psychologist for chilling reason' - NewsBreak
text:
By Edward Easton Jane Lavender ,
35 minutes ago A woman who spent her childhood yearning to be blind has shared how a psychologist manipulated her into pouring drain cleaner into her eyes.
Jewel Shuping, hailing from North Carolina, asserted that she was afflicted with Body Integrity Identity Disorder (BIID), a condition where individuals believe they are destined to have a disability.

As a child, she would gaze at the sun for hours after being told it could harm her vision.
As a teenager, she started wearing dark sunglasses and began learning braille, decisions she referred to as "blind-swimming", essentially pretending to live life without sight.
She described the urges she experienced as overpowering. "The idea kept coming up in my head and by the time I was 21 it was a non-stop alarm that was going off," she admitted.
In 2006, she journeyed to Chicago to meet a man who purported to be a psychologist.
According to Shuping, he secluded her in his home for two weeks, instructing her not to reach out to family or friends, reports the Mirror .
He then positioned her and used a syringe to drip potent drain cleaner into her eyes.
"He had me stay in his home for two weeks, telling me not to contact family or friends," she later penned in an online post.
"Then one day, he laid me down and used a rubber syringe to put drain cleaner in my eyes."
She further revealed that he made her wait half an hour before escorting her to the hospital.
Ultimately, the damage took months to completely rob her of her sight.
Despite informing reporters at the time that the disturbing actions of the psychologist, who has never been publicly identified, were consensual, in a recent post on internet forum Reddit she revealed she now believes this may not have been accurate.
"The memories of wanting to be blind as a child were false ones, reality twisted to suit the narrative," she wrote.
"I do not believe I would have ever considered blindness under any circumstances."
She also claimed the man exploited her by reinterpreting traumatic childhood experiences as evidence she "wanted" blindness.
"He would point to that and tell me this was me wanting to be blinded," she said.
Shuping says she has since received extensive trauma therapy and now struggles with complex PTSD and social anxiety.
"What this man did to me haunts me to this day," she wrote.
